## Fixed

- Keep Close and Minimize responsive by bounding Accessibility button calls and fallback window capture with the command's shared deadline and cancellation.
- Preserve known minimized windows and native tab groups when a temporary Accessibility read fails.
- Retire stale window entries when a process ID is reused, while preserving state when process identity is temporarily unavailable.
- Give every pending window a restoration attempt when slow windows consume a batch's time budget.
- Avoid recalculating unchanged taskbars for activity on another display, while preserving resizing, dragging and explicit icon updates.
- Release command tokens for retired windows instead of retaining them until the app stops.
- Show the correct name and icon for separate application installations that share a bundle identifier.
- Remove unused production wrappers and exclude test-only feedback observation from Release builds.

## Verification

Adds 26 behavior regressions, including cancellation, deadline exhaustion, native tabs, process generations, restoration fairness, resource origins and bounded caches. The reviewed local source passes 955 tests and 202 lifecycle/regression repeats with a constrained Swift executor. Python, Node.js and WindowLab replay checks pass. Independent repeat review has no unresolved actionable findings. The restoration fairness regression allows the bounded number of batches required by the pending-window count, so it remains valid on slower CI runners.

This release is published only after the existing CI workflow reruns its full test, constrained-executor, replay, compatibility and Apple Silicon package checks for the release commit.

No new runtime dependencies, settings, permissions or persistent background tasks are introduced. Real CPU/RAM/energy and native third-party-app acceptance were not measured in the local review.
